title: Social Media and Modern Communication
learningObjectives: Learn vocabulary related to social media platforms and online interaction
Understand the impact of social media on society and communication
Practice discussing digital citizenship and online safety
Recognize terms related to content creation and digital marketing

sections.title: The Social Media Revolution
sections.content:
Social media has transformed how we communicate, share information, and connect with others. Platforms like Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, TikTok, and LinkedIn have billions of users worldwide. Understanding social media vocabulary is essential in today's digital age, whether for personal use, professional networking, or business marketing.

This lesson explores the language of social media, its benefits and challenges, and how to navigate the digital world responsibly.

sections.title: Social Media Platforms and Features
sections.content:
Different platforms serve different purposes. Facebook connects people through <posts>, <photos>, and <status updates>. Instagram focuses on visual content with stories that disappear after 24 hours. Twitter uses short tweets with hashtags. TikTok features short-form videos. LinkedIn is for professional networking.

Common features: like, comment, share, follow users, <tag> people, and send <direct messages> (DMs). Your <profile> shows your information. <Notifications> alert you to activity.

sections.title: Creating and Sharing Content
sections.content:
<Content creators> or influencers produce material for audiences. They post regularly to maintain engagement - likes, comments, and shares. Viral content spreads rapidly across the internet.

<Algorithms> determine what users see in their feed. Hashtags help reach wider audiences. <Live streaming> broadcasts video in real-time.

Filters and <editing tools> enhance photos and videos. Building a following takes consistent quality content. <Analytics> track metrics like reach and <engagement rate>.

sections.title: Social Media's Impact and Challenges
sections.content:
Social media offers benefits: staying connected, accessing information, and business opportunities. However, <cyberbullying> harms people online. <Misinformation> and <fake news> spread quickly.

<Privacy concerns> arise from data collection. Addiction affects mental health. <Echo chambers> expose users only to similar viewpoints.

<Doomscrolling> means endlessly consuming negative news. Set time limits, verify information before sharing, and remember that online personas don't show complete reality.

sections.title: Social Media Conversations
sections.content:
Example 1: DISCUSSING USAGE - <I spend too much time scrolling through Instagram. I need to limit my screen time.>

Example 2: CONTENT CREATION - <I'm trying to grow my following on TikTok by posting daily videos with trending hashtags.>

Example 3: PRIVACY CONCERN - <I'm worried about my privacy. I've adjusted my settings to limit who can see my posts.>

sections.title: Digital Wellbeing and Screen Time
sections.content:
As social media becomes central to daily life, <digital wellbeing> is an important topic. Excessive screen time can affect mental health, sleep, and relationships.

• <Screen time> - Time spent using digital devices
• <Digital detox> - Taking a break from technology
• <FOMO> - Anxiety that others are having better experiences
• <Doomscrolling> - Continuously reading negative news
• <Notification fatigue> - Feeling overwhelmed by alerts

Strategies: set daily <time limits>, turn off non-essential notifications, avoid screens before bed, and schedule <offline activities>.

sections.title: Social Media Scenarios
sections.content:
Example 1: ONLINE REPUTATION - <A friend posted an embarrassing photo of me without asking. I asked her to take it down. It's important to respect privacy online.>

Example 2: MISINFORMATION - <I saw a shocking headline but the source turned out to be false. Always verify information before sharing.>

Example 3: DIGITAL BALANCE - <I used to check my phone first thing every morning. Now I wait until after breakfast. It's made my mornings more peaceful.>

sections.title: Digital Citizenship
sections.content:
Social media is a powerful tool that requires responsible use. Key vocabulary includes platform names, features (post, like, share, follow), and concepts (viral, algorithm, influencer). Be a good <digital citizen>: think before you post, respect others, verify information, protect your privacy, and maintain healthy boundaries.

Remember that social media shows curated versions of reality - don't compare your life to others' highlight reels. Use these platforms to connect meaningfully, learn, and share positively. Balance online and offline life for better well-being.

keyVocabulary.definition: A person with the power to affect others' purchasing decisions or opinions
keyVocabulary.example: Many brands partner with influencers for marketing campaigns.

keyVocabulary.definition: Content that spreads rapidly and widely across the internet
keyVocabulary.example: Her video went viral and got millions of views.

keyVocabulary.definition: A set of rules that determines what content users see
keyVocabulary.example: The algorithm shows you posts based on your interests.

keyVocabulary.definition: Interaction with content through likes, comments, and shares
keyVocabulary.example: High engagement rates indicate popular content.

keyVocabulary.definition: A word or phrase preceded by # to categorize content
keyVocabulary.example: Use relevant hashtags to increase your post's visibility.

keyVocabulary.definition: Bullying that takes place online or through digital devices
keyVocabulary.example: Schools are working to prevent cyberbullying among students.

grammarPoints.rule: Social Media Verbs and Phrasal Verbs
grammarPoints.explanation: Social media has created new verbs and uses of existing ones.
examples: post/upload - I posted a photo on Instagram.
scroll through - I was scrolling through my feed.
commonMistakes: Using "make" instead of "post": "I made a post" ❌ → "I posted" ✓

grammarPoints.rule: Discussing Social Media Trends and Impact
grammarPoints.explanation: Use present perfect for recent trends and present continuous for ongoing situations.
examples: Social media has changed how we communicate. (impact)
More people are becoming aware of privacy issues. (trend)
commonMistakes: Using simple past for ongoing relevance: "Social media changed" vs "has changed" (still relevant)
